findings.body:
**Do not describe an abandoned operation as terminated.**

`src/kernel/README.md:147-149` says the runner detaches the promise. That does not stop the underlying operation, which can continue consuming resources or incurring spend. State that the invocation settles while the operation may continue.
findings.title: Do not describe an abandoned operation as terminated.

findings.body:
**Do not imply an input change resets the budget.**

`src/kernel/README.md:218-224` says governed runs seed attempts and spend from the plan’s history. Changing `inputsHash` defeats replay skipping, but it does not clear a tripped governor or reset the job’s attempt count. Remove the claim that an input change puts work back under the caps.
findings.title: Do not imply an input change resets the budget.

findings.body:
**Add `capabilityEvidence` to the strict-ceiling infrastructure-failure verdict.**

Line 830 says the rg probe evidence is attached to "EVERY post-probe verdict from this run". This return is the only post-probe verdict in `runObserved` that omits `...capabilityEvidence`. The sibling paths include it: the abort return (Line 1300), the ceiling `budget` return (Line 1318), and the generic error return (Line 1354). The equivalent repair-path infrastructure return in `settleStructuredMiss` also includes it (Line 1810).

This is the trigger. A strict-budget run probes rg, and then the capability or durable hook fails (`err.kind !== 'budget'`). The resulting `WorkerResult` then has no `capabilities.rg` and no `advisories`. A consumer therefore loses the "search tools unavailable" note on that verdict, although the probe ran.

<details>
<summary>Proposed fix</summary>

```diff
         return {
           usage: stepUsage,
           usageProvenance: usageEvidence ? 'measured' : 'unmeasured',
           steps: completedSteps,
           sessionId: record.sessionId,
           denials,
+          ...capabilityEvidence,
           stopReason: 'error',
           error: boundedErrorText(
```
</details>
findings.title: Add `capabilityEvidence` to the strict-ceiling infrastructure-failure verdict.

findings.body:
**Prefer the `id: 'model'` entry before the category fallback.**

The docstring at protocol.ts:625-626 makes `id: 'model'` the primary match and `category: 'model'` the fallback. The single `find` at Line 635 returns the first entry that matches either condition. Consider an array that lists a `category: 'model'` entry with a different id (for example, a secondary or draft-model option) before the `id: 'model'` entry. In that case, the function returns the wrong `currentValue`, and the driver reports the wrong served model for the run. Search for the exact id first. Use the category match only when no entry has that id.

<details>
<summary>🐛 Proposed fix</summary>

```diff
-  const option = configOptions?.find((entry) => entry.id === 'model' || entry.category === 'model');
+  const option =
+    configOptions?.find((entry) => entry.id === 'model') ??
+    configOptions?.find((entry) => entry.category === 'model');
```
</details>
findings.title: Prefer the `id: 'model'` entry before the category fallback.

findings.body:
**SIGKILL fires at `src/driver/acp/process.ts:284` against a child that already exited on SIGTERM.**

`closed()` waits for `close`, not `exit`. `close` waits for stdio to end. A grandchild that inherited the piped stdio can keep `close` pending after the child has exited on SIGTERM. In that case the ladder does the following:
- It waits the full `termGraceMs`.
- It records a `sigkill` rung marker.
- It calls `child.kill('SIGKILL')` on a dead process, which is a silent no-op.
- It returns `'killed'`.

The header (Line 236) promises "the markers stay honest", but the marker and outcome are wrong here.

Check `isAcpProcessExited(child)` after each grace window expires.

<details>
<summary>Proposed fix</summary>

```diff
   if (await closesWithin(termGraceMs)) {
     return 'terminated';
   }
+  if (isAcpProcessExited(child)) {
+    return 'terminated'; // exited in the window; only stdio close is pending
+  }
```
</details>
findings.title: SIGKILL fires at `src/driver/acp/process.ts:284` against a child that already exited on SIGTERM.
